why: The authors' official repo is present and its entrypoint (main.py --dataset ml-1m --k 148) is exactly the pipeline behind C1, and k=148 matches the paper's gamma=0.04 x min(|U|,|I|)=3706. But it cannot run as released on this machine: requirements.txt pins torch==1.11.0+cu113, jax/jaxlib==0.3.25 and neural-tangents==0.6.1, none of which have wheels for Python 3.12, and the preprocessed data is a Google Drive zip that may not be fetchable. Since SVD-AE is a closed-form truncated SVD, the authors' model logic (symmetric normalization -> truncated SVD -> score) is a few dozen lines we can port to scipy/numpy or modern torch while keeping the authors' code path intact. The only real uncertainty is the exact train/validation/test split, which lives in the Google Drive archive.
missing_artifacts: data.zip preprocessed datasets (ML-1M/ML-10M/Gowalla/Yelp2018) hosted on Google Drive - availability not guaranteed
exact per-user train/validation/test split used for Table 2 (falls out of data.zip; otherwise must be regenerated and becomes a source of variance on HR@10 31.79)
blockers_seen: jax==0.3.25 / jaxlib==0.3.25 pinned; no wheels for Python 3.12 on Windows
neural-tangents==0.6.1 is tied to the old jax version
preprocessed data only distributed via a Google Drive link, no in-repo data and no raw-data prep script for the paper's split
repo targets Python 3.9 / CUDA 11.4; GPU is irrelevant to the math but the pinned stack is not installable here

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: About 10-20 minutes total: ~3-5 min to install a working modern stack (numpy/scipy/torch cpu) and skip the dead pins, ~2 min to obtain ML-1M and build the normalized 6040x3706 matrix (or ~10 s if data.zip downloads), under 1 min for the rank-148 truncated SVD, ~2-3 min for the full leave-one-out/held-out ranking evaluation over 6040 users, plus one clean re-run.

compute.basis: Closed-form rank-148 truncated SVD of a 6040x3706 sparse matrix plus full ranking evaluation on 6040 ML-1M users - seconds to a couple of minutes of CPU per run, dominated by install and data download.
